CPDAG of a known directed structure

Source: R/metrics.R
mc_true_cpdag.Rd

Builds the completed partially directed acyclic graph (CPDAG) of the equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) given through the structural matrix of the modified Cholesky parametrization, where a nonzero \(T_{ji}\) codes the arc \(i \to j\). The equivalence class is the set of DAGs with the same skeleton and the same v-structures (Verma and Pearl, 1990; Andersson, Madigan and Perlman, 1997). The v-structures are written first and Meek's rules complete the orientation, which gives the object an estimated CPDAG should be compared against.

Usage

mc_true_cpdag(T, tol = 0)

Arguments

T

a finite numeric square matrix whose entry \((j, i)\) is nonzero when \(i \to j\); the structural matrix of the directed layer is one such, and the transpose of a directed adjacency is another.

tol

non-negative number; entries not above it in absolute value count as zero (default 0).

Value

The adjacency matrix of the CPDAG, in the package convention (see mc_cpdag_metrics), with the dimnames of T.

Arcs anywhere, not only below the diagonal

A structural matrix of the modified Cholesky parametrization is lower triangular, so its arcs run from a lower index to a higher one and reading only the lower triangle would suffice. A DAG that arrives from elsewhere need not be numbered in a topological order, and its arcs can sit anywhere, so every off-diagonal entry is read. For a triangular input the two readings agree. A pair carrying an arc in both directions, or a set of arcs with a cycle, is refused.

References

Verma, T. and Pearl, J. (1990). Equivalence and synthesis of causal models. Proceedings of the Sixth Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 220–227.

Andersson, S. A., Madigan, D. and Perlman, M. D. (1997). A characterization of Markov equivalence classes for acyclic digraphs. The Annals of Statistics 25(2), 505–541. doi:10.1214/aos/1031833662

See also

mc_cpdag_metrics.

Other structure recovery: mc_cpdag_metrics(), mc_structure_metrics()

Examples

T <- diag(3)
T[3, 1] <- -0.5; T[3, 2] <- -0.4        # 1 -> 3 <- 2, a collider
mc_true_cpdag(T)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    0    0    1
#> [2,]    0    0    1
#> [3,]    0    0    0
